$meta.title: The five machines
$meta.description: What each AC6502 system is, what is onboard, what is optional, and what is absent. Unlike the rest of data/, this file is hand-maintained: the KiCad repos' READMEs are structured too differently to parse, so each record was authored from its README and carried verified:false until Phase 3 confirmed it against the schematics (SCHEM). Every per-system record now carries verified:true with a SCHEM citation; the one exception is the shared architecture block below, which is GREP-sourced and out of this pass's scope.

shared.description: Every AC6502 machine shares these, which is why one BIOS serves all five.
shared.cpu: 65C02, or a cycle-accurate emulation of one
shared.memory: 32 KB RAM + 32 KB ROM, with optional banked RAM expansion
shared.memoryMap: Standardised across the family — see data/memory-map.json
shared.bus: 16-bit address bus, 8-bit bidirectional data bus, standard 65C02 control signals (RW, PHI2, RESET, IRQ, NMI, RDY, SYNC)
shared.bios: The common BIOS provides the Kernal, Monitor and BASIC on every machine

systems.name: ACE
systems.tagline: The whole family on one board.
systems.summary: A complete, self-contained 65C02 computer on a single PCB. It integrates everything found across the COB's modular cards — CPU, memory, video, audio, storage, serial, GPIO, RTC and keyboard controller — onto one board, delivering the full experience without a backplane or expansion cards.

onboard.detail: Battery-backed clock and 256 bytes of NVRAM
J6 JOYSTICK A on VIA PORT A reads as JOY(2); J8 JOYSTICK B on VIA PORT B reads as JOY(1)
Drives the ATmega1284 at 16 MHz and the 65C02 at 1 or 2 MHz via a 74HC163 divider
Manual reset into the ATmega1284, which also provides power-on reset to the 65C02

optional.detail: 512 KB, as 256 × 1 KB windows per half
CompactFlash in 8-bit True IDE mode, into the Storage header

boards.name: ACE CF Adapter
boards.detail: CompactFlash adapter for the Storage header

boards.name: ACE RAM Patch
boards.detail: Piggyback fix for Rev 1.0 banked RAM; plugs into the U13 socket

revisions.notes: Fixes the LOADL/LOADH latch-enable gating for the banked SRAM: the final NAND stage becomes a NOR (LOADL = NOR(SEL_L, WB)), added as one 74HC02 (U23). Pull-ups R1–R4 and R25 go from 1 kΩ to 10 kΩ; C31 (10 µF) added at the power input. No firmware change.
Initial release. Banked RAM does not latch reliably — needs the ACE RAM Patch.

systems.check: SCHEM — Hardware/ACE Board/Rev 1.0 and Rev 1.1, Hardware/ACE CF Adapter/Rev 1.0 (6502-ACE.kicad_sch): confirms W65C02S, AS6C62256, AT28C256, Pico9918, 6581/ARMSID, 65C51+MAX238, 65C22, DS1511Y, AS6C4008, ATmega1284-P, PS/2 connector, X1, SW70, J1/J6/J8. Rev 1.1 revision note confirmed directly: R1-R4/R25 read 1k in Rev 1.0 and 10k in Rev 1.1, C31 (10uF) exists only in Rev 1.1, and U23 (74HC02) appears four times in Rev 1.1 driving the LOADL/LOADH global labels the note describes, absent from Rev 1.0.

systems.name: COB
systems.tagline: Build the machine you want, one card at a time.
systems.summary: The modular machine. A passive backplane carries the bus; every function — CPU, memory, video, sound, storage, serial, GPIO, RTC — is a card you choose to fit or leave out. This is the system the BIOS's hardware probe exists for.

optional.detail: Hosts the 65C02 in card form
65816 16-bit CPU, backward-compatible with the 65C02
32 KB SRAM + 32 KB EEPROM with address decoding
512 KB as two 256 KB banks, 256 × 1 KB windows each
DS1511Y with battery backup and 256 bytes of NVRAM
CompactFlash over IDE
SD card + 16 MB SPI flash
optional.status: untested — the stock BIOS has no driver for it

optional.detail: RS-232 via 65C51 ACIA + MAX232
Adds full modem control (DTR, DCD, DSR)
65C22 VIA for keyboards, joysticks, timers
3-voice SID via ARMSID, RCA line-level out
VGA 640×480 via Pico9918
Fully programmable VGA via Pi Pico
Composite video via a real TMS9918A with 16 KB VRAM
Enhanced composite video
16×2 character LCD via 65C22 VIA, 4- or 8-bit mode
LEDs on the 16 address, 8 data and 8 control lines, live
Breadboard area with full bus access

boards.name: Backplane Pro
boards.detail: 5 slots plus integrated clock, reset and power distribution. Rev 1.1 is all through-hole and adds a power switch and DC barrel jack.

boards.name: Backplane Helper
boards.detail: Expands the total configuration to as many as 12 slots

revisions.notes: Entirely through-hole; adds an onboard power switch and DC barrel jack input.

systems.check: SCHEM — every card under Hardware/ confirms its claimed chip (65C02/65C816 CPU cards, AS6C62256+AT28C256 Memory Card, AS6C4008 RAM Card, DS1511Y RTC Card, CompactFlash Storage Card, W25Q128JVS+microSD Storage Card Pro, 65C51+MAX232 Serial Card/Pro with DTR/DCD/DSR, 65C22 GPIO Card, Pico9918A VGA Card/Pro, TMS9918A Video Card, 65C22+16x2 LCD Card, 6581-socket Sound Card). Backplane Pro Rev 1.1 confirmed: adds a Barrel_Jack_Switch + POWER switch absent from Rev 1.0, and nearly every passive switches from _SMD to _THT footprints, matching "entirely through-hole" plus the power switch/barrel jack. Slot numbers (1-8) are not silkscreen-labelled in any schematic, so those remain sourced from the README rather than SCHEM.

systems.name: DEV
systems.tagline: A 65C02 you can single-step, with the peripherals emulated alongside.
systems.summary: An emulation-based development system. It replaces the physical 65C02 with a Teensy 4.1 running cycle-accurate 65C02 emulation via vrEmu6502, and adds hardware Run/Stop, Step, Reset and Frequency controls — so the bus can be stopped and inspected in a way real silicon will not allow.

onboard.detail: Cycle-accurate 65C02 emulation driving a real bus
Level shifters onto a real 6502 bus connector and card slot

optional.detail: Teensy 4.0 + 2.4" ILI9341 TFT emulating a TMS9918A and a 6581 SID, driven over high-speed serial. The DEV Board sends the same AV packets over USB simultaneously, so a browser can render the output in parallel.
Level-shifted, for driving genuine COB cards

absent.reason: Emulated by the Teensy — this is the point of the board

systems.check: SCHEM — Hardware/DEV Board/Rev 1.0/DEV Board.kicad_sch confirms the Teensy 4.1, exactly 5 SN74LVC4245APWR level shifters (U1/U2/U3/U5/U6), SW1-SW4 labelled Run/Stop, Step, Clock, Reset respectively, an RJ45 Ethernet jack, a CR2032 holder, and a USB-C USB Host receptacle. Hardware/DEV Output Board/Rev 1.0/DEV Output Board.kicad_sch confirms the Teensy 4.0 and a Waveshare 2.4in LCD module (the schematic doesn't name the driver IC, so "ILI9341" is the module's known datasheet part rather than a schematic-visible string); no TMS9918/6581 part strings appear since both are software-emulated on the Teensy 4.0, consistent with the design.

systems.name: KIM
systems.tagline: 24 keys, two lines of LCD, and nothing in the way.
systems.formFactor: Minimal machine — backplane build (preferred) or single Main Board
systems.emulationNote: The Keypad Card overlays the top of the address space, replacing BASIC, the Monitor, Wozmon and the CPU vectors. Neither the emulator nor the DEV board models that takeover, so the KIM is not currently emulated.
systems.summary: A KIM-1-inspired minimal computer. The preferred build is a COB Backplane (or Backplane Pro) with the COB CPU Card, Memory Card, Serial Card and Backplane Helper, plus the Keypad Card that the Keypad Helper and Keypad LCD Helper attach to. The VCS Main Board can stand in for the Backplane/CPU/Memory combination.

optional.detail: Preferred build
Preferred build
Preferred build
Carries the concurrent Wozmon-compatible serial monitor

65C21 PIA, AT28C64 8 KB EEPROM, two 74HC138 decoders. Port A carries the keypad code (PA0–PA4) and the LCD control lines (PA5 = RS, PA6 = R/W, PA7 = E); Port B is the LCD data bus. CA1 is the keypad data-available interrupt, CA2 the encoder's output enable.
24 Cherry MX switches as a 4×6 matrix, MM74C922 16-key encoder extended to 24 with a 74HC00. All scanning, debounce and encoding in hardware — no microcontroller, no firmware.
16×2 HD44780 with a 10 kΩ contrast trimmer; passes PA0–PA4, CA1 and CA2 through to the Keypad Helper.
Replaces Backplane + CPU Card + Memory Card

absent.reason: The KIM's display is the 16×2 LCD

absent.role: BASIC / Monitor / Wozmon at their usual addresses
absent.reason: The Keypad Card's ROM overlays $E000–$FFFF and the vectors

memoryOverlay.description: Unlike every other card in the family, the Keypad Card overlays the top of the address space. The BIOS Kernal stays reachable and the cartridge calls into it.
memoryOverlay.check: SCHEM — Keypad Card's 74HC138 U1 decodes A13-A15; its Y6 output ($C000-$DFFF, 8 KB granularity) drives net PEB into the 65C21's CS2B, and net REB (from the same decode stage) gates both the AT28C64's CE and OE, consistent with a contiguous ROM block at the top of the map. The precise $E000-$FFF9 vs $FFFA-$FFFF vector split could not be traced to a single decoder output pin-for-pin (likely additional glue logic), so that exact boundary remains sourced from the README rather than fully pin-traced.

firmware.name: KC Monitor
firmware.detail: 6502 assembly cartridge ROM burned to the Keypad Card's AT28C64. Turns the card into a KIM-1-style hex monitor — browse and edit memory, execute code from the 24-key keypad and 16×2 LCD — with a concurrent Wozmon-compatible serial monitor when a Serial Card is fitted.

systems.check: SCHEM — Keypad Card confirms 65C21 PIA, AT28C64, two 74HC138 decoders. Keypad Helper confirms 24 Cherry MX switches (SW1-SW24) in a matrix into an MM74C922, extended by a 74HC00. Keypad LCD Helper confirms a 16×2 LCD connector and a 10 kΩ trimmer. Pin-traced (not just label text) through the connector geometry: PA0-PA4/CA1/CA2 pass unchanged from the Keypad Card through the LCD Helper to the Keypad Helper; the LCD Helper remaps PA5/PA6/PA7 to RS/R-W/E exactly as documented; CA1/CA2 land on the MM74C922's DA (data-available) and XOE (output-enable) pins exactly as documented.

systems.name: VCS
systems.tagline: Plug in a cartridge, pick up a joystick.
systems.formFactor: Cartridge console — Main, Input and Output boards
systems.summary: A cartridge-based retro gaming console with a real 65C02, swappable ROM cartridges, VGA video via Pico9918, SID audio via ARMSID, and support for PS/2 keyboards, matrix keyboards and Atari 2600-compatible joysticks.

onboard.detail: On the Input Board; the ATmega1284p is the keyboard encoder controller
They share the VIA ports with the keyboard encoder rather than having connectors of their own: J1 PORT B reads as JOY(1), J2 PORT A reads as JOY(2).

optional.detail: 28C256 32 KB EEPROM — electrically erasable, no UV eraser needed
27C256 32 KB EPROM — UV-erasable

absent.reason: No CompactFlash — programs arrive on cartridge

boards.name: Main Board
boards.detail: 65C02, 32 KB SRAM, 32 KB EEPROM, clock and reset; carries the bus for the Input and Output boards

boards.name: Input Board
boards.detail: Matrix keyboard, PS/2 keyboard and joysticks over a 65C22 VIA with an ATmega1284p encoder

revisions.notes: Pull-up resistors changed from 1 kΩ to 10 kΩ.

systems.check: SCHEM — Main Board confirms 65C02 (U6), AS6C62256 (U2), AT28C256 (U3). Output Board confirms Pico9918A and a DIP-28 6581-compatible socket (ARMSID is the socketed part, not a schematic-visible string — same pattern as the ACE board). Input Board confirms 65C22 (U1) and ATmega1284-P, and — the highest-risk claim in this record — the J1/J2-to-VIA-port mapping is confirmed exactly: J1's Value property is "PORT B", J2's is "PORT A", matching "J1 PORT B reads as JOY(1), J2 PORT A reads as JOY(2)" verbatim. ROM Cart Rev 1.0a/1.0b confirm AT28C256/AT27C256 respectively. Main Board Rev 1.0→1.1 confirmed: R10-R14 all read 1k in Rev 1.0 and 10k in Rev 1.1 (R8 stays 10k in both, R1/R9 stay 1k in both), the same pull-up bump already confirmed on ACE.
